title: Composition of orientations and of tensor maps
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be smooth separated morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $h=gf$.

Use either a finite commutative ring $A$ with $\ell^rA=0$ for some $r\geq1$, and the ordinary constant-$A$ pro-etale derived categories and bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories of [det-sp-finite-general-ring], or the coefficient system $B=A_\bullet=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_{n\geq1}$ for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, in the ordinary derived categories of varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] and their uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. In the finite case write $B=A$. Write $\mathcal C_T(B)$ for the respective constructible finite-Tor category. An input tower need not be normalized. All tensor products are ordinary derived tensor products over $B$, including in the tower case.

Use pullback, tensor, twists and shifts as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-tensor, def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with arbitrary finite-$A$ twists as in [det-sp-finite-general-ring] and levelwise twists for towers. Put $d_f=d$, $d_g=e$, $d_h=d+e$. For $u=f,g,h$ let $F_u=Ru_{!,B}\dashv G_u=u_B^!$ and $\omega_u=G_uB_{\mathrm{target}(u)}$; use [det-sp-finite-general-ring, def-pur-co-smoothness] at finite coefficients and [det-sp-tower-gluing, det-sp-tower-gamma] for towers. Write $L_u=B_{\mathrm{source}(u)}(d_u)[2d_u]$ and $a_u:L_u\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_u$ for the inverse diagonal orientation, and $t_{u,L}:u^*L\otimes^L\omega_u\to G_uL$ for the canonical tensor map, adjoint to inverse projection followed by $1_L\otimes\varepsilon_{u,1}$. Thus $\gamma_u(L)=t_{u,L}(1\otimes a_u)$ after twist reassociation [def-pur-smooth-purity-map, det-sp-finite-general-ring, det-sp-tower-gamma]. Let $c:G_h\xrightarrow{\sim}G_fG_g$ be the adjunction-preserving compositor of [det-sp-composition-comparisons]. Set
$$W=f^*\omega_g\otimes^L\omega_f,\qquad \rho=t_{f,\omega_g}:W\xrightarrow{\sim}G_f\omega_g,\qquad \mu=\rho^{-1}c_1:\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}W.$$
Then:

1. Under the canonical shifted-Tate tensor splitting $L_h=B_X(d+e)[2d+2e]\simeq f^*L_g\otimes^LL_f$, the orientations satisfy
$$\mu a_h=f^*a_g\otimes a_f.$$
Equivalently the orientation $\omega_h\to L_h$ is the product of the two orientations under $\mu$.
2. For every $K\in\mathcal C_Z(B)$, under pullback composition and tensor reassociation,
$$c_K\,t_{h,K}(1\otimes\mu^{-1})=t_{f,G_gK}(f^*t_{g,K}\otimes1_{\omega_f})$$
as maps $h^*K\otimes^LW\to G_fG_gK$.

Consequently
$$c_K\,\gamma_h(K)=\gamma_f(G_gK)\circ f^*(\gamma_g(K))(d)[2d]$$
under the same canonical twist, shift and pullback identifications.

proof.text: All schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the field $k$ (whose only ideals are $0,k$). Their separated finite-type structure maps make them quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies compactifications for $f,g,h$. Domains and notation. The composition $h$ is smooth of relative dimension $d+e$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2). The finite purity isomorphisms of [det-sp-finite-general-ring](1),(3) give $\omega_u\simeq B(d_u)[2d_u]$ and $G_uK\simeq u^*K(d_u)[2d_u]$ in the stated finite-Tor categories. For towers the same statements, with uniform bounds and natural maps in the ordinary derived tower category, are [det-sp-tower-gamma](1),(2). Thus $\omega_g$, $G_gK$, $W$ and the sources of both sides are legitimate inputs; in particular $\rho$ is invertible. Tensor invertibility and finite Tor bounds of the lines follow from [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] and scalar extension [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](2),(3). Tensoring locally with a free line preserves a specified Tor interval; a shift by $[2d]$ subtracts $2d$ from its endpoints, uniformly at every tower level. We use no normalization hypothesis on $K_\bullet$.

Projection composition on the actual coefficient categories. Use the order $\operatorname{PF}_{u,M,L}:F_uM\otimes L\to F_u(M\otimes u^*L)$. Its composition identity at finite $A$ is [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition] on ordinary etale coefficients, transported, including counits and the specified projection transformations, by [lem-pur-finite-ring-site-tensor-transpose](1),(2). The statement of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], at the identity coefficient map $A\to A$, says explicitly that the same site comparison intertwines the canonical compact-support composition identifications; thus the transported projection identity uses the required compositor. For towers use the arbitrary-system identity of [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate], before evaluation. Its uniformizer indexing may be restricted to the subsequence $en$, where $e$ is the ramification index: $(\varpi_E^{en})=(\ell^n)$, so its quotient systems and actual section-model maps become precisely the $\ell$-power ones. The identity has no normalization hypothesis. Invertibility of the tower projection maps on our uniform finite-Tor inputs is [lem-sp-tower-compact-support-projection-formula]. Write $q_{u,L}:F_u(u^*L\otimes\omega_u)\to L$ for inverse projection (including symmetry) followed by $\varepsilon_{u,1}\otimes1_L$. These are the transposes defining $t$ in [det-sp-finite-general-ring] and [det-sp-tower-gamma](2).

source.place: (2): projection formula composition, including the actual tower maps

proof.text:
Compare the transposes for clause (2). Put $P=h^*K\otimes W$ and $s=\varepsilon_{g,1}\circ F_g(q_{f,\omega_g}):F_gF_fW\to B_Z$. Transposing the iterated tensor map first under $F_f\dashv G_f$ and then under $F_g\dashv G_g$ replaces each $t$ by its defining $q$. Naturality of the counits and the projections, and associativity of $\operatorname{PF}$ in its tensor variable, $\operatorname{PF}_{u,M,L\otimes L'}=\operatorname{PF}_{u,M\otimes u^*L,L'}(\operatorname{PF}_{u,M,L}\otimes1)$ (proper part: [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition] on the ringed topoi of constant $A$ or of $\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet$-towers [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian](1); for $j_!$ both sides transpose under $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ to $\eta\otimes1\otimes1$), applied with $M=\omega_f$, $L=\omega_g$, $L'=g^*K$, give
$$F_gF_fP\xrightarrow{\mathrm{sym},\,\operatorname{PF}_{\mathrm{comp}}^{-1}}F_gF_fW\otimes K\xrightarrow{s\otimes1}K,$$
where $\operatorname{PF}_{\mathrm{comp}}=F_g(\operatorname{PF}_{f,W,g^*K})\operatorname{PF}_{g,F_fW,K}$, with symmetry moving $K$ last.
For the other map, use $\alpha:F_gF_f\simeq F_h$ and $c=\theta:G_h\simeq G_fG_g$ of [det-sp-composition-comparisons](1), or (3) for towers. Their adjunction normalization says
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{comp}}_K\circ F_gF_f(c_K)=\varepsilon_{h,K}\circ\alpha_{G_hK},\qquad \varepsilon^{\mathrm{comp}}_K=\varepsilon_{g,K}\circ F_g(\varepsilon_{f,G_gK}).$$
Since $c_1\mu^{-1}=\rho$ and $\varepsilon_{f,\omega_g}F_f(\rho)=q_{f,\omega_g}$, naturality of $\alpha$ identifies the resulting counit on $W$ with
$$\varepsilon_{h,1}F_h(\mu^{-1})\alpha_W=\varepsilon^{\mathrm{comp}}_1F_gF_f(\rho)=s.$$
Step 2 identifies the inverse projection for $h$ with $\operatorname{PF}_{\mathrm{comp}}^{-1}$ through this same $\alpha$. Thus the transpose of $c_Kt_{h,K}(1\otimes\mu^{-1})$ is the displayed map too. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves clause (2), in the tower derived category itself too.

Choose nested affine charts, first with coefficients $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$. By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], for every $x\in X$ choose affine opens $S\subset Z$, $V\subset g^{-1}S$ about $f(x)$ and $U\subset f^{-1}V$ about $x$, and etale maps $v:V\to\mathbf A^e_S$ and $u:U\to\mathbf A^d_V$. The map $b:\mathbf A^d_V\to\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_S}$ is the base change of $v$, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Its composite $bu$ is etale by the dimension-zero case of [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2). Thus $h|_U=p_{d+e,S}bu$ is a chart with ordered $d$-block followed by $e$-block. All bases used for the affine-space law below are affine, hence separated. The chart maps are separated: their diagonals are pullbacks of those of the separated structure morphisms to $k$. Here [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) gives separatedness of the affine bases; [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) give the asserted closed diagonals. The etale chart maps are of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), since their sources are affine and targets separated. Restricting a finite-type $k$-scheme to these affine opens remains finite type by restriction of its locally finite-type structure map and quasi-compactness of an affine source. Thus the chart lemmas apply on their stated finite-type domains.

On these $R$-charts the diagonal orientations are the canonical adjunction orientations of [det-sp-orientation-charts]. Open restriction, the etale identification $e^!=e^*$, and tensor/base-change comparisons are those of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](1),(3),(4) and [lem-pur-co-smooth-etale-locality]. Consequently the restriction of
$$\rho(f^*a_g\otimes a_f):f^*L_g\otimes L_f\longrightarrow G_fG_gR_Z$$
is the pullback along $bu$ of
$$\Gamma_{p_d,G_{p_e}R}\circ p_d^*(\Gamma_{p_e,R})(d)[2d].$$
To see the factors explicitly, replace $a_g|_V$ by $v^*\Gamma_{p_e,R}$ and $a_f|_U$ by $u^*\Gamma_{p_{d,V},R}$. The base-change square defining $b$ carries the tensor map for $p_{d,V}$ at $v^*\omega_{p_e}$ to $b^*$ of the tensor map for $p_d$ at $\omega_{p_e}$; its source and the two line factors are identified by monoidal pullback. Source-etale restriction along $u$ gives the displayed composite. The same chart formula identifies $a_h|_U$ with $(bu)^*\Gamma_{p_{d+e},R}$. For $d,e\geq1$, [prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law] equates these maps with their counit-preserving exceptional compositors. Thus $c_1a_h=\rho(f^*a_g\otimes a_f)$ on $U$. The sign from interchanging the shifted line blocks is $(-1)^{(2d)(2e)}=1$. Here $\Gamma_{p_d,L}=t_{p_d,L}(1\otimes\Gamma_{p_d,1})$ for every $L\in D^b_{ctf}$ on the affine base, and $a_{p}=\Gamma_{p,1}$: [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] identifies the smooth purity map of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] (inverse diagonal orientation followed by the tensor map) with $\Gamma_{p_d}$, and at the unit $t_{p_d,1}$ is the unit identification. The same node identifies the maps $\gamma_{p_d}$ of [prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law] with $\Gamma_{p_d}$ for $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and it gives the normalization of $\vartheta^{\mathrm{aff}}$ in [det-sp-orientation-charts]. We use it with $L=\omega_{p_e}=G_{p_e}R$, which lies in $D^b_{ctf}$.

source.place: (1): ordered affine integration on the nested charts

proof.text: The zero-dimensional blocks require no positive-dimensional affine-space lemma. By [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement], $\Gamma_{p_0,K}=1_K$ and the ordered $d$-space comparison is the recursive composite of $d$ line comparisons. If $d=0$ or $e=0$, deleting the empty block gives literally that same composite with the tensor unit and identity compositor. The chart normalization [det-sp-orientation-charts] includes $d=0$; the etale tensor formula of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] and [lem-pur-co-smooth-etale-locality] identifies the remaining etale factor with inverse image. Therefore the local equation of Step 5 holds also in these cases, including $d=e=0$.

Globalize the orientation equation at $R$. Compose both local maps of Step 5 with $\rho^{-1}$ and the inverse product orientation. They become endomorphisms of $R_X(d+e)[2d+2e]$. After removing the common shift these are maps between degree-zero sheaves, by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]. They agree on the open cover by the $U$ of Step 4, so uniqueness in [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] makes them equal globally. Undoing the invertible factors gives $\mu a_h=f^*a_g\otimes a_f$ for $R$. Substituting this into clause (2), already proved in Step 3, and $\gamma_u=t_u(1\otimes a_u)$ gives the purity-composition equation at $R$, in particular at the coefficient unit. This is an equation about specified normalized orientations, not merely an isomorphism between their endpoints. Here $t_{u,1}$ is the unit identification: its transpose is exactly $\varepsilon_{u,1}$, since projection with the coefficient unit is the tensor unitor. The adjunction bijection sends $1_{G_u1}$ to that counit. Hence $\gamma_u(1)=a_u$.

source.place: (1): local-to-global equality of shifted sheaf maps

proof.text:
Pass the unit equation from $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ to any finite commutative $A$ with $\ell^rA=0$. Write $S=(-)_A$, $r_u(L):S G_{u,R}L\xrightarrow\sim G_{u,A}(SL)$ for the exceptional coefficient comparison, and $c_R,c_A$ for the geometric compositors. The explicit second equation of [det-sp-composition-comparisons](2), with its coefficient rings specialized to $R\to A$, is
$$c_A(SK)r_h(K)=G_{f,A}(r_g(K))\,r_f(G_{g,R}K)\,S(c_R(K)).$$
Here $K=R_Z$ and $G_{g,R}K$ meet the constructible finite-Tor hypotheses by Step 1. By [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](3), $r_u(L)S(\gamma_{u,R}(L))=\gamma_{u,A}(SL)$. Apply these equations to Step 7. Naturality of $\gamma_{f,A}$ in the isomorphism $r_g(R_Z)$ moves $G_{f,A}(r_g(R_Z))$ across $\gamma_{f,A}(SG_{g,R}R_Z)$. The chart assertion of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] identifies the sources with the canonical scalar, twist and pullback comparisons. The resulting equation is
$$c_A(A_Z)a_{h,A}=\gamma_{f,A}(G_{g,A}A_Z)\circ f_A^*(a_{g,A})(d)[2d]=\rho_A(f_A^*a_{g,A}\otimes a_{f,A}).$$
The last equality expands $\gamma_f=t_f(1\otimes a_f)$ from [det-sp-finite-general-ring](3). Clauses (1),(2) of that node identify each $a_{u,A}=r_u(R)S(a_{u,R})$ with the direct diagonal orientation. Thus $\mu_Aa_{h,A}=f_A^*a_{g,A}\otimes a_{f,A}$. No flatness of $A$ over $R$ is used; scalar extension is derived.

source.place: (1): arbitrary finite admissible rings via normalized coefficient comparisons

proof.text: Orientation equality for towers. The two arrows $\mu a_h$ and $f^*a_g\otimes a_f$ exist in the ordinary derived tower category by [det-sp-tower-gamma] and [det-sp-composition-comparisons](3). Clause (3) supplies actual compositors on uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor towers, and identifies their evaluations with the finite $\alpha_{A_n},\theta_{A_n}$ including counit normalization; it does not require input normalization. Thus the level $n$ evaluations of our arrows are the finite orientation arrows with $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$; [det-sp-tower-gluing](3) preserves their adjunction units and counits. For $t$ this also follows by cancelling $1\otimes a_u$ from $\gamma_u=t_u(1\otimes a_u)$, since both $a_u$ and $\gamma_u$ have their specified finite evaluations. Step 8 equates those finite arrows. Both endpoints are concentrated in degree $-2(d+e)$: each orientation identifies its dualizing object with its shifted Tate line, and locally the unshifted tensor of two free lines is a degree-zero sheaf. Evaluation is exact and computes cohomology levelwise by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian](1),(2), so vanishing in other degrees is detected on all levels. By [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] remove the common shift, and by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identify these maps with actual maps of tower sheaves. Such maps are componentwise families by [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Their equality at every level therefore gives their equality as tower-sheaf maps, and hence in the derived tower category. This proves clause (1) without asserting faithfulness of evaluation for general derived maps.

source.place: (1): equality of shifted rank-one tower-sheaf maps

proof.text:
Finish at arbitrary $K$ in either coefficient setting. Naturality of the counit-defined tensor map follows by transposing its natural inverse-projection/counit composite; the relevant maps are those of [det-sp-finite-general-ring](3) and [det-sp-tower-gamma](2). In Step 3 replace $\mu^{-1}(f^*a_g\otimes a_f)$ by $a_h$, using Steps 8 and 9. This gives
$$c_K\gamma_h(K)=t_{f,G_gK}\bigl(f^*(t_{g,K}(1\otimes a_g))\otimes a_f\bigr).$$
Expanding $\gamma_f$ and $\gamma_g$ rewrites the right side as $\gamma_f(G_gK)\circ f^*(\gamma_g(K))(d)[2d]$. The rebracketing, shift and twist identifications are those in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]; all shifted line degrees are even, so their interchange has sign $+1$. This proves the consequence while retaining the separate orientation and tensor identities.

Expanded the inverse-projection/counit computation, checked nested affine charts including dimension zero, extended the prime-power orientation equality using the existing coefficient comparisons, and tested tower orientation equality only after reducing to shifted tower sheaves. Reused existing nodes; no new nodes or Lean edits. tool_uses.why: The actual compact-support projection composition identity at arbitrary finite rings is the generic input to the tensor-transpose calculation.
Carries the actual finite projection maps and counits from the ordinary etale site to the pro-etale site; no purity-composition conclusion is used.
Supplies composition of the specified projection transformations in arbitrary strict systems, before evaluation and without normalization.
Supplies invertibility of actual tower projection maps on uniform constructible finite-Tor inputs.
Identifies degree-zero derived arrows with sheaf arrows for local-to-global and tower equality tests.
Reduces concentrated tower complexes to shifted objects of their abelian category.
Uniqueness for module-sheaf maps on the affine chart cover globalizes the prime-power orientation equation.
Supplies degree-zero free Tate lines and their finite reductions for domain and tower concentration checks.
Gives the dimension of the composite and the etaleness of composite coordinate maps.
Produces the nested etale affine-space charts used by the unit orientation argument.
Gives the etale base-changed coordinate map b used to form the full chart.
Names the actual tower orientation and counit-defined tensor map, their finite evaluations and uniform constructible finite-Tor domains; no composition-of-purity assertion is imported.
Verifies Noetherianity for the ordinary etale tensor-composition tool, rather than silently assuming its hypothesis.
Verifies that affine target charts are separated, as required by the affine comparison law.
The closed-diagonal base-change clause checks separatedness of the coordinate maps.
Checks finite presentation and hence finite type of the affine-source etale coordinate maps.
Ensures that finite etale-to-pro-etale transport intertwines the actual compact-support compositor, in addition to the projection/counit compatibility already cited.

Associativity of the proper projection maps in the tensor variable on ringed topoi; it is needed for the compact-support projection maps in the transpose calculation, and no node of the unit states it.
Open restriction, etale composition and base change of the canonical tensor map on the nested charts; this is the orientation-free tensor-formula interface.
Etale maps have trivial dualizing object, which identifies chart restrictions with inverse images.
Existence of compactifications, a hypothesis of the compact-support projection-composition identity.
Exact level evaluation, and the tower category as modules in a ringed topos of inverse systems, for the tower heart argument and the projection associativity.
